```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
analysis_dir <- "."
metrics <- read_csv(file.path(analysis_dir, "summary_statistics.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
participants <- read_csv(file.path(analysis_dir, "participant_statistics.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
events <- read_csv("../final_stage_events.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
active_n <- sum(!is.na(participants$duration))
sensor_n <- nrow(participants)
dur <- participants$duration[!is.na(participants$duration)]
ici <- participants$median_interclap_interval[!is.na(participants$median_interclap_interval)]
```

## Data at a glance

The motion files contain 50 Hz accelerometer-derived signals for `r sensor_n` participant sensors. `r active_n` participants have defined start/end times and durations in the supplied statistics table. The remaining `r sensor_n - active_n` participants have no defined clapping interval and are not included in timing summaries.

The supplied notes describe sensor time alignment as accurate to approximately 100 ms on average, and stage-event times as accurate to within about half a second. Treat short timing differences cautiously.

## Timeline and ensemble activity

The heatmap shows the trimmed motion series, with participants ordered by their detected clapping start time. Red vertical lines mark stage events. A missing/blank region means no retained observation, not zero motion.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(analysis_dir, "figure_participant_timeline.png"))
```

The line below summarizes the median normalized motion across participants at each time point; the shaded band is the interquartile range. These are descriptive summaries, not confidence intervals.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(analysis_dir, "figure_ensemble_activity.png"))
```

## Participant timing statistics

```{r}
kable(metrics %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 2))),
      caption = "Descriptive statistics for supplied participant-level measures")
```

Among participants with defined durations, the median duration was **`r round(median(dur), 1)` seconds** (IQR `r round(quantile(dur, .25), 1)`–`r round(quantile(dur, .75), 1)`). The median of participant median interclap intervals was **`r round(median(ici), 2)` seconds**, equivalent to approximately **`r round(60 / median(ici))` claps per minute**. This rate is a reciprocal transformation of the median interval; it is not the average applause rate of the whole crowd.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(analysis_dir, "figure_duration_distribution.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(analysis_dir, "figure_interclap_intervals.png"))
```

## Exploratory relation between interval and motion

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(analysis_dir, "figure_interval_vs_rms.png"))
```

This plot is exploratory and uses participant-level summary measures. Motion values are normalized sensor measures, not calibrated physical acceleration or sound level.

## Stage events

```{r}
kable(events, col.names = c("Time (seconds)", "Event"), caption = "Annotated stage events")
```

## Interpretation cautions

- The data describe clapping by instrumented participants; the concert-hall audio also contains claps from non-participant audience members.
- Signals are median-normalized, so their magnitude should not be read as absolute force or loudness.
- Empty cells are missing observations, and the trimmed data intentionally blank periods outside each participant's detected clapping interval.
- Participant-level summary distributions describe the instrumented participants only. They are not estimates of audience-wide behavior.
- No inferential tests are included in this visual summary; the data notes do not document a sampling design or population-level model.
